title: Change some `wmem_packet_scope()` to `pinfo->pool`
description:
As requested [here][1] by @eapache1, help replace calls to
`wmem_packet_scope()` with references to `pinfo->pool`.

My principles were:

* Plugins chosen semi-randomly and favouring minimal size of changes.
* When a calling function already has a `pinfo` argument, just use that.
    * Remove `_U_` from its signature if it was there.
* If the allocated value is only used within the function, change it to
  use a NULL allocator and free it when done.
* Favour changing the calling signature of only static functions.
    * Don't go more than 2 or 3 levels deep of changing signatures.
* When a non-static function is changed, it was chosen for minimal usage
  outside of the affected dissector.
* No mention of `wmem_packet_scope()` should remain in the files I
  changed.

The first of several similar MRs that will come as time allows.

[1]: https://www.wireshark.org/lists/wireshark-dev/202107/msg00052.html

added 8 commits
  • ae1c598c...e69446aa - 7 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 21366703 - Change some `wmem_packet_scope()` to `pinfo->pool`
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/3767/diffs?diff_id=220564455&start_sha=ae1c598cc9810f8888cb7665cad936aedc1875e4)

Thanks David. Most of this makes sense to me, but I think “If the allocated value is only used within the function, change it to use a NULL allocator and free it when done.” is mistaken. These allocations should still use the pinfo pool in order to avoid memory leaks when Wireshark aborts packet dissection in the middle of a method. Given that the memory has to be allocated as part of a pool anyway, the manual frees are not typically worth doing.

Noted, thanks. I'll give it another pass on Wednesday. That'll mean a notable increase in passing around `pinfo` or `pinfo->pool` through a few layers of functions, though; there are several places where `wmem_packet_scope()` is used for a temporary value that never leaves the calling function.
I did this tonight. There are a few cases where `wmem_packet_scope()` is used in functions that are callbacks to glib functions, so I just put those back the way they were.

commits_data.title: Rework to avoid NULL allocation pool
commits_data.message:
Rework to avoid NULL allocation pool

Rework my previous commit to no longer use a NULL allocation pool.

In most cases this involved changing function signatures and passing
`pinfo` to more functions.

In a few cases this meant reverting my work entirely since the function
involved was a callback with a signature set by glib.
